div.head: Cn 1020 1
div.ab: Cnut cyning gret his arcebiscopas ⁊ his leodbiscopas ⁊ Þurcyl eorl ⁊ ealle his eorlas ⁊ ealne his þeodscype, twelfhynde ⁊ twyhynde, gehadode ⁊ læwede, on Englalande freondlice.
King Canute sends friendly greetings to his archbishops and his diocesan bishops and Earl Thurkil and all his earls and all his subjects in England, nobles and commoners, ecclesiastics and laymen.

King Cnut greets in friendship his archbishops and his diocesan bishops, and Earl Thorkel and all his earls, and all his people, whether men of a twelve hundred wergild or a two hundred, ecclesiastic and lay, in England.

König Cnut grüsst seine Erzbischöfe und seine Suffragan-Bischöfe und Thurkil, Herzog [von Ostanglien] und alle seine Grafen und sein ganzes Volk — von 1200 und 200 [Schilling Wergeld], Geistliche und Laien — in England freundlich.

King Cnut greets his archbishops and his diocesan bishops and Earl Thorkell [of East Anglia] and all his earls and all his people — of 1200 and 200 [shillings' wergild], clergy and laity — in England in friendship.
div.note: Only source: the York Gospels (York Minster), copied c. 1030–70 on a blank flyleaf after homilies (Wulfstan ed. Napier no. 59 ff.) that repeat pieces of Æthelred's and Cnut's laws. Dated 1020, February–July.

The MS. uses an abbreviation that is usually singular; but in chap. 8 the same abbreviation is used when the accompanying possessive shows that the plural “archbishops” is intended, and doubtless this is meant here also.
